name: Can You Live in the House During a Garage Addition?

mainEntity.name: Can a garage addition be built while the house is occupied in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: Can a garage addition be built while the house is occupied in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many homeowners stay in the house during a garage addition, but the project should be planned to minimize disruption. Detached garages are usually easier to build while occupied because most of the work happens outside the main living space. Even so, construction can affect parking, deliveries, noise, dust, and access around the property. If the project is attached or requires utility tie-ins close to the home, the impact may be greater. A contractor should explain how the site will be protected, where workers will access the property, and whether temporary driveway or parking changes are needed. In Los Angeles County, neighborhood tightness and limited lot space can make logistics especially important. The safest approach is to discuss daily routines, pets, children, and vehicle access before construction begins so the contractor can plan around them.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many garage additions can be built while the home is occupied, especially if the garage is detached or access can be separated from daily living areas. The main concerns are noise, dust, equipment access, parking disruption, and safety around the work zone.
